newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares taken aback at open by Dow weakness.
newsitem.headline: German shares taken aback at open by Dow weakness.

text.p: German shares were quoted lower in early trade on Friday, shaken by the size of an overnight slump in share prices on Wall Street and on hold before U.S. jobs numbers due later in the day.
The blue-chip DAX index fell 9.15 points, or 0.36 percent, to 2,520.39 shortly after opening amid trade described by one dealer as "very calm".
"People were a bit surprised by the strength of the correction on Wall Street," another said, referring to the 0.88 percent dip in the Dow Jones Industrial index on Thursday.
Others nonetheless pointed to the relative resilience of German shares, with the stability of the dollar against the mark providing some support.
Both DAX and Bund futures were however quoted lower before the next focus of market attention, U.S. unemployment and payrolls data due at 1230 GMT on Friday.
Economist forecasts on average see U.S. unemployment falling slightly to 5.3 percent in August, with August payrolls seen up 244,000 on average.
Individual share movements were limited. Shares in electronics group Siemens AG gained 49 pfennigs to 78.46 after a large buy-order early in the morning, dealers said.
Shares in commercial bank Deutsche Bank AG continued their recent weakness, slipping 63 pfennigs to 71.72.

Deutsche was quoted in London's Financial Times newspaper as admitting to control failings in its British asset management arm Morgan Grenfell, three of whose European funds were suspended earlier this week on suspected irregularities.
Trading in the funds has since resumed after Deutsche bought a total 180 million pounds of the funds' securities for its own account.
